paper_metadata.title: Rasengan: A Transition Hamiltonian-based Approximation Algorithm for Solving Constrained Binary Optimization Problems

summary: Rasengan is a gate-based variational quantum algorithm for constrained binary optimization, evaluated on 20 benchmark instances across five problem families and on IBM Kyiv/Brisbane devices for small cases. The paper reports ARG improvements of 4.12x over the best quantum baseline, circuit depth reductions from about 7000 to about 50, and a 379x improvement on real hardware versus the feasible-solution baseline, but it does not demonstrate a practical classical advantage.

experiments.description: Rasengan transition-Hamiltonian VQA evaluated algorithmically on five constrained binary optimization benchmarks (facility location, k-partition, job scheduling, set cover, graph coloring) against HEA, penalty-based QAOA, and Choco-Q in noise-free simulation.

algorithm.optimizer: constrained optimization by linear approximation (COBYLA-like method cited as Powell's method in refs)

hyperparameters.transition_hamiltonian_rounds: m^2 total simulations for totally unimodular matrices; up to m^3 for more complex cases
hyperparameters.segment_depth_target: single transition Hamiltonian per segment after optimization

algorithm.parameter_initialization: initial state set to one arbitrary feasible solution

problem_formulation.encoding_details: binary variables encoded on qubits; Rasengan starts from one feasible basis state and expands via homogeneous basis vectors under transition Hamiltonians
problem_formulation.objective_function: min or max f(x) subject to Cx = b, x in {0,1}^n
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: hard constraints preserved by transition Hamiltonian; purification removes infeasible outputs after each segment
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: transition Hamiltonian H^T(u) derived from homogeneous basis vectors; objective Hamiltonian not used in Rasengan

problem_instance.description: Five benchmark families: facility location, k-partition, job scheduling, set cover, graph coloring; 20 benchmark instances summarized in Table 2 and 2000 cases across five domains in the abstract
problem_instance.dataset_name: facility location, k-partition, job scheduling, set cover, graph coloring

dataset_specification.description: 400 cases from relevant literature per benchmark family; Table 2 reports 20 benchmark instances (F1-F4, K1-K4, J1-J4, S1-S4, G1-G4)

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: feasible solution constructed greedily or trivially per problem family; homogeneous basis derived from constraint matrix; basis simplification/pruning applied
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: noise-free simulation over benchmark suite; ARG, circuit depth, and parameter count reported; scalability analysis on increasing FLP sizes; ablation studies; 100 iterations on real hardware for small-scale problems

implementation_details.transpilation_target: IBM Quebec model; DDSim for Rasengan circuit simulation; Qiskit Aer GPU used for baselines
implementation_details.classical_solver: constrained optimization by linear approximation (Powell 1994 cited)
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: construct one feasible solution; compute homogeneous basis from linear constraints; greedy basis simplification and pruning; segment partitioning; purification after each segment
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: measure basis states; compute ARG and in-constraints rate; remove infeasible states during purification

speedup_claims.conditions: algorithmic evaluation across 2000 cases from five benchmark families in noise-free simulation
speedup_claims.caveats: Paper uses approximation ratio gap (ARG), where lower is better; this is an improvement in solution quality, not a runtime speedup.

speedup_claims.baseline_method: prior works on real IBM quantum devices
speedup_claims.conditions: real-device runs on IBM-Kyiv and IBM-Brisbane for small instances F1, K1, J1
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper does not specify a single baseline method for this aggregate claim in the excerpt; it refers to the average quality of feasible solutions on hardware.
Depth varies by benchmark; this is the maximum reported relative reduction.

This is an internal optimization claim, not a comparison to an external baseline.

speedup_claims.conditions: after purification-based error mitigation on hardware

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: transition Hamiltonian simulation decomposes to linear complexity in number of nonzero basis-vector elements; upper bound 34nm^2 CX gates for full sequence, or 34nm^3 in more complex cases
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: feasible solution construction is O(d), O(e), O(j), O(s), or O(g) depending on benchmark; basis simplification O(m^2 n)

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not established; reported improvements are benchmark-specific and do not show asymptotic crossover
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Up to 78 qubits in scalability analysis; 8-24 qubits in Table 2; IBM superconducting QPUs for small instances
limiting_factors: Performance is compared mainly against other VQAs, not strong classical optimization solvers
Circuit depth and noise remain limiting on hardware

notes: Rasengan is a gate-based variational quantum algorithm; no quantum annealer experiments are included.

Hardware is reported as IBM cloud devices (Kyiv, Brisbane) for real-device runs and Qiskit/DDSim simulation for algorithmic evaluation; this experiment entry summarizes the main algorithmic evaluation and scalability results, not the hardware-only subset.
The paper does not provide a single fixed qubit count or depth because they vary by benchmark; ranges were extracted from Table 2 and scalability figures.

The paper reports 4.12x better ARG than the best quantum baseline (Choco-Q) and 379x improvement on real hardware versus the feasible-solution baseline, but does not establish a classical advantage over state-of-the-art classical optimization.

experiments.description: Noise sensitivity analysis of Rasengan under depolarizing/phase damping and amplitude damping noise models on simulated circuits.

algorithm.optimizer: constrained optimization by linear approximation (Powell's method cited)

key_results: Under Pauli noise rates around 1e-3, more than 99% of ARGs are below 0.025.
At 0.001 error rate, average ARG remains below 0.15.
With amplitude damping probability increasing from 0% to 1.5%, ARG increases only slightly; at 2% intermediate states from segmented execution can become infeasible.

experiments.description: Ablation study of optimization strategies: Hamiltonian simplification, Hamiltonian pruning, and segmented execution with purification.
key_results: Average circuit depth reductions of 9.8%, 67%, and 82% for simplification, pruning, and segmented execution respectively.
Opt 2 improves ARG by 1.18x on simulators and 1.37x on hardware.
Opt 3 further boosts ARG by 2.43x, and purification yields a 303x improvement on hardware.
In-constraints rate reaches 100% at the algorithmic level.

experiments.description: Hamiltonian pruning evaluation on FLP, KPP, SCP, and GCP showing faster coverage of feasible solution space.
key_results: For the fourth scale, unpruned chains require 73.6% of total chain length to cover the feasible space, while pruned chains require 40.7%, a 1.8x speedup.
